english.title: Motor vehicle fail to comply with endorsable section 36 traffic sign - automatic equipment
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), drove a motor vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), and failed to comply with the indication given by a traffic sign specified as subject to obligatory endorsement in Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988, namely

(A)_[a height limit sign,]_
(B)_[a level crossing slow/large vehicle phone to cross sign,]_
(C)_[light signals for the control of road traffic at a level crossing,]_
(D)_[light signals for the control of road traffic at a swing or lifting bridge,]_
(E)_[light signals for the control of road traffic at an airfield,]_
(F)_[light signals for the control of road traffic in the vicinity of premises used regularly by fire and rescue authority, police or ambulance vehicles,]_
(G)_[a school crossing patrol stop sign,]_
(H)_[zig-zag lines at a Puffin crossing, signal-controlled crossing facility or portable signal-controlled pedestrian facility,]_
(I)_[zig-zag lines at a Zebra crossing,]_
(J)_[zig-zag lines at a Parallel pedestrian and cyclist crossing,]_
(K)_[a no entry sign,]_

lawfully placed on or near a road, namely **(..SPECIFY ROAD AND LOCATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 36(1) of the Road Traffic Act 1988, the Traffic Signs Regulations and General Directions 2016 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

english.notes:
(i) See offence document H19028 for the same offence detected by manned equipment
(ii) Offence documents H12688 - H12693 cater for the contravention of stop signs, traffic lights and solid white line road markings
(iii) Non-endorsable section 36 traffic signs are catered for by offence documents H12682 (ACD) and H12683 (non-ACD)
(iv) No Entry signs
In order to prosecute a driver for failing to comply with a no entry sign, there must be a Traffic Regulation Order (TRO) in place for the sign.
(v) The Traffic Signs Regulations and General Directions 2016, resulted in 'No Entry' signs being no longer endorsable section 36 road traffic signs. The Traffic Signs (Amendment England and Wales) Regulations and General Directions 2017 have rectified the situation and from 13 December 2017 'No Entry' signs are again classed as endorsable section 36 road traffic signs.
